description: >-
                Deterministic identifier shared by owners in the same household: the first 12
                lower-case hex characters of the SHA-256 of '<lastName>|<postcode>', with the last
                name trimmed, whitespace-collapsed and lower-cased. Owners with the same last name and
                postcode therefore always share it. Absent for owners without a postcode.
              type: string
              example: '3f2b8c1e7a4d'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                Derived identity used for duplicate detection, formatted as
                '<telephone>|<email>|<householdId>' from the normalized telephone, the lower-cased
                email (empty when absent) and the household ID (empty when absent). Creating an owner
                whose whole identity key equals an existing owner's is rejected with 409 Conflict;
                owners differing in any part, e.g. household members with different telephones, are
                allowed.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                Assigned on create: the number of owners that already existed before this owner was
                created with the same first name and last name, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 0

Deleting an owner is now a soft-delete, and the full test suite passes (`./mvnw test`: 18 tests, 0 failures), including the two acceptance tests for this change.

**What it does now**
- `DELETE /api/owners/{id}` sets the owner's `deleted` flag to true and keeps the row. It still returns 204, or 404 if the owner doesn't exist.
- `GET /api/owners/{id}` still returns a deleted owner, with `"deleted": true`. A newly created owner has `"deleted": false`.
- When creating an owner, both blocking checks skip deleted owners: the household check (409 `DuplicateHousehold`) and the identity-key check (409 `DuplicateIdentity`). So re-creating an owner whose only match was deleted now succeeds.

**Main changes**
- `Owner.java`: new `deleted` field. All four database schemas (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) get a `deleted BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` column, so the existing seed data loads unchanged.
- `ClinicServiceImpl.deleteOwner` now sets the flag and saves instead of deleting the record.
- `OwnerRepository`: new `countNotDeletedByHouseholdId`, used for the household check. I implemented it in all three repository versions (Spring Data, JPA, JDBC). The JDBC version also reads and writes the new column.
- `openapi.yml`: added `deleted` to the Owner schema and changed the DELETE description to say it's a soft-delete.

**Decisions for you**
- **Possible-duplicate flag:** I also made the non-blocking `possibleDuplicateOf` marker skip deleted owners, since it's a duplicate check too. Otherwise a new owner could be pointed at a deleted one. This is easy to undo if you'd rather it still counted them.
- **Checks I left alone:** these still count deleted owners: city capacity, the daily owner limit, customer-code uniqueness, namesake count and household size. Customer-code uniqueness has to, because the rows still exist. The others could go either way; I left them because the spec only covered duplicate and identity checks.
- **Owner lists:** listing and search endpoints still include deleted owners, since the spec didn't say to hide them.
- **Other profiles:** I also ran the acceptance tests with the JDBC and JPA profiles selected and they passed. But I didn't confirm the profile override actually took effect, so treat those two as unconfirmed.
